excerpts.text:
Rootfs is a special instance of ramfs (or tmpfs, if that's enabled), which is
always present in 2.6 systems.  You can't unmount rootfs for approximately the
same reason you can't kill the init process; rather than having special code
to check for and handle an empty list, it's smaller and simpler for the kernel
to just make sure certain lists can't become empty.

Most systems just mount another filesystem over rootfs and ignore it.  The
amount of space an empty instance of ramfs takes up is tiny.

- When switching another root device, initrd would pivot_root and then
    umount the ramdisk.  But initramfs is rootfs: you can neither pivot_root
    rootfs, nor unmount it.  Instead delete everything out of rootfs to
    free up the space (find -xdev / -exec rm '{}' ';'), overmount rootfs
    with the new root (cd /newmount; mount --move . /; chroot .), attach
    stdin/stdout/stderr to the new /dev/console, and exec the new init.

    Since this is a remarkably persnickety process (and involves deleting
    commands before you can run them), the klibc package introduced a helper
    program (utils/run_init.c) to do all this for you.  Most other packages
    (such as busybox) have named this command "switch_root".
#ifdef CONFIG_TMPFS_XATTR

#ifdef CONFIG_TMPFS_XATTR
	.listxattr	= shmem_listxattr,
	.fileattr_get	= shmem_fileattr_get,
	.fileattr_set	= shmem_fileattr_set,
#endif
#ifdef CONFIG_TMPFS_POSIX_ACL
	.setattr	= shmem_setattr,
	.set_acl	= simple_set_acl,
#endif
};

conclusions.denied_permission: The candidate new inode SID var_t is checked against the superblock SID root_t for filesystem associate after the caller's ordinary relabel permissions.
conclusions.rootfs_sid_origin: security_fs_use keys on sb->s_type->name. The rootfs type has no fsuse entry in the fixed policy and uses genfscon rootfs / root_t.
conclusions.initial_rootfs_backend: With the observed nonempty root= and rootfstype=ext4, init_rootfs leaves is_tmpfs false and the rootfs wrapper uses the ramfs initializer. Its s_type name remains rootfs.

pre_policy_remount_fscontext_rejected.earliest_rejection: selinux_add_opt sees !selinux_initialized before allocating or retaining mount options.

conclusions.post_policy_remount_fscontext_rejected: bad_option rejects a new FSCONTEXT_MNT flag or different SID on the initialized superblock; selinux_sb_remount is a compatibility check, not a SID setter.

prior_closure_inspection_failure.cause: Expected loader in usr/lib64; actual ordinary loader is usr/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1. No kernel or target program executed.

source_behavior.api_mount_move_failure_handling: Warn and try forced unmount; missing/already-mounted destination takes a detach branch. Later bootstrap/runtime guards must validate API filesystems.
root_change_sequence: parent closes its own old-root fd

next_stage_required_proofs: Run only as the guarded PID 1 in the dedicated initramfs, before the first SELinux policy load.
Keep /init bytes and the fixed Enforcing policy unchanged; add an independent stage0/stage1 contract.

Mount a genuinely new ordinary tmpfs superblock without context/fscontext/rootcontext overrides; preserve qualified payloads, symlinks, modes and hardlink topology while excluding API mounts and the new-root destination from copy.
Preserve a non-CLOEXEC old-root directory FD, require its filesystem magic to be RAMFS or TMPFS, and require its st_dev to differ from the new TMPFS root.
Ensure SIGCHLD is not ignored and SA_NOCLDWAIT is not set before switch_root forks.
Wait for and reap the actual cleanup child before policy loading; a zero child status alone is insufficient.
Enumerate the inherited old-root directory to EOF without error, permitting only . and .., then close it before executing the frozen native bootstrap.
Treat an empty old-root directory as an empty named tree, not an exact measurement of freed physical pages or proof that no other descriptor holds an unlinked inode.
Preserve archive, firmware, executable, loaded-policy, actual initrd-domain, no-AVC, descriptor-passing and event-transfer runtime gates in the independent next candidate.
